narrative.intro: The federal government obligated $14.7B in contracts by NAICS for FY2027 to date. Facilities Support Services led the market with $3.8B in obligations. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) accounted for $1.2B, and Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers also accounted for $1.2B. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences recorded $1.1B. Computer Systems Design Services, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, and Other Computer Related Services followed with $786M, $766M, and $720M respectively. Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists) received $462M. Engineering Services received $457M. Security Guards and Patrol Services received $411M. These figures reflect obligations recorded so far in the fiscal year and do not represent a full-year total. Contractors and acquisition planners should treat the listed totals as current-year-to-date obligations when comparing markets or allocating pursuit resources. The ranking shows a mix of services, professional R&D, construction, health, and security spending concentrated in the top NAICS sectors.

sections.heading: Which industries hold the largest share of FY2027 obligations by NAICS?
sections.body: Facilities Support Services holds the largest dollar total with $3.8B in obligations. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) and Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers each have $1.2B in obligations. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences has $1.1B, followed by Computer Systems Design Services at $786M and Commercial and Institutional Building Construction at $766M.

sections.heading: How is spending distributed across professional services, construction, and health sectors?
sections.body: Professional services and R&D appear prominently with Research and Development entries and Computer Systems Design Services totaling $1.1B and $786M respectively. Construction appears through Commercial and Institutional Building Construction at $766M. Health and medical-related NAICS include Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers at $1.2B and Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists) at $462M.

faq.q: What are the biggest federal contracting industries?
faq.a: Facilities Support Services is the biggest federal contracting industry, with $3.8B in obligations. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) and Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers each have $1.2B in obligations. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences has $1.1B. Other notable industries include Computer Systems Design Services at $786M, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction at $766M, Other Computer Related Services at $720M, Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists) at $462M, Engineering Services at $457M, and Security Guards and Patrol Services at $411M.
